description:
MATERIAL. Every token is built from one vocabulary: flat, semi-transparent convex polygons -- overwhelmingly hexagons, with some pentagons and rounded heptagons -- layered many deep over a near-black ground. Where they overlap the translucency stacks, so the picture is made of plateaus and seams rather than outlines; there are no strokes, no line work, no text, no texture fills. The edges are noticeably soft at 512px, as if the whole frame were rendered slightly out of focus or upscaled; at 256 that softness reads as a deliberate haze, at 120 it reads as blur.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. A rosette. Each frame is a radially symmetric mandala of roughly six-fold symmetry centred exactly in the frame -- a rose window, or a honeycomb seen through a kaleidoscope, or a pollen grain / spore cluster under a lens. The square corners are consistently cut to black because the rosette is inscribed in a hexagonal-circular boundary, which gives every token the same dark-cornered, medallion-in-a-square silhouette. The centre is always the subject: it is either a large soft khaki-grey disc (1203347, 1475115, 1733538, and 1243682 in a smaller version) or a spiral/ring scatter of small dark dots that read as seeds, spores or bacterial colonies (1283437, 1310661, 1835793, 1991107, and 1561509).

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. The palette, the polygon vocabulary, the centred radial symmetry, the black-cornered medallion silhouette, the soft edges, and the plan: a differentiated core inside an annulus of hexagons that bleeds off all four edges. Colour is essentially warm-monochrome -- burnt terracotta through salmon-tan to rust-brown, all within a narrow hue band -- plus black ground, plus one desaturated olive/khaki-grey that carries the central disc and the small dots. There is no second colour and no cool note anywhere in the twelve.

HOW THEY DIFFER. Almost entirely by what the centre does and how much black is allowed to show. Two seeds invert the scheme completely and are the obvious outliers: 1446330 and 1561509 are black-dominant, with orange hexagons scattered as discrete confetti across the whole field out to the edges rather than massed into a plate. 1366079 is nearly empty -- a pale unbroken field with a single tiny black point dead centre and a few faint specks. The remaining nine are variations of one plan, and three of them (1203347, 1475115, 1733538) are close to interchangeable: orange field, khaki blob centre, black corner wedges. The differences that do exist are of scale and density -- how big the core is, how coarse the surrounding hexagons are -- not of structure.

ACROSS THE THREE STATES (seen for 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661). The consistent gesture is that STRESS opens a black void at the centre and raises contrast, while RECOVERY refills the centre with mass or dots and returns the frame to warm and even. It is strongest in 1243682, where stress replaces the neutral dark octagon with a hard black star-shaped halo that is unmistakable even at 120px, and recovery fills that halo with a mottled khaki plate. 1310661 is the second clearest: neutral is a loose scatter of dots, stress collapses to a black hexagonal void with a small ring in it, recovery re-blooms into a dotted lattice. 1283437 tightens its dot spiral under stress and adds concentric dark banding, then spreads the dots wider and larger in recovery. 1203347 is the weak one: at 120px its three states are nearly the same picture -- an orange field with a khaki blob -- with only a slight change in the blob's edge and in how much black shows between the outer hexagons.

WHAT SURVIVES AT 120px. The medallion silhouette, the black corners, the warm ground and the presence or absence of a dark core all survive. What does not survive is anything inside the core: the dot clusters of 1283437, 1310661, 1835793 and 1991107 collapse into a single speckled grey smudge, and the difference between a dotted core and a solid core is nearly the only distinction left. The twelve sort into about four visible families at browse size -- orange field with khaki blob (1203347, 1475115, 1733538), orange field with speckled core (1283437, 1310661, 1835793, 1991107, 1985692), black confetti field (1446330, 1561509), and near-empty pale field (1366079) -- rather than twelve individuals.

OTHER THINGS I NOTICE. The black corner wedges in 1203347, 1243682 and 1985692 have hard straight cuts that read more like a boundary the shapes were clipped against than like a chosen edge. In 1366079 a single tiny black dot sits exactly at centre and reads as a pinprick artifact rather than a mark. The khaki-grey of the cores is a low-value step away from the surrounding orange, so the core often looks fogged rather than drawn. Nothing in any frame dominates except the centre, and the surrounding field is an even, unhierarchical carpet of repeated hexagons.
